mobile.notifications.answer.note: Button on an ask in the inbox list that opens it to be answered. One word, imperative.

mobile.notifications.back.note: Accessibility label of the icon-only back button in the inbox header.

It is the name of one of Local Operator's built-in notification sounds; use the same translation as the desktop app's sound picker (wire.notification_sound.sound.*). Sentence case, no final full stop.

mobile.notifications.computer_registrati.note: Settings › Notifications, a status line: registering this phone for the computer's push notifications failed for a temporary reason; the app retries when it is opened again.

Settings › Notifications, a status line: the phone's operating system has not given the app a push address (device token), so the computer cannot send push notifications to it. 'Reopen the app' is the remedy.
Settings › Notifications, a status line: the computer has revoked or unpaired this phone for push notifications; only the computer's owner can allow it again, from the computer.
Settings › Notifications, a status line: the computer the phone is connected to has accepted this phone as a place to send its push notifications. Must not promise that alerts will definitely arrive.

Settings › Notifications, a status line while the phone is sending its registration to the computer it is connected to. 'Alerts' are push notifications from that computer (an agent finished, a conversation needs attention).
Settings › Notifications, a status line: the computer runs an older Local Operator (product name, keep in Latin script) that cannot register phones for push notifications.

mobile.notifications.detail.answer_in_co.note: Primary button on an ask's detail view that opens the conversation where the ask can be answered. Sentence case, no final full stop.

mobile.notifications.detail.conversation.note: Section header listing the asks raised in the notification's conversation. "Ask" is the product word for a question the agent puts to the reader.

mobile.notifications.detail.earlier_upda.note: Section header listing earlier revisions of the same notification.

mobile.notifications.detail.from.note: Section header naming the conversation a notification came from. One word.

mobile.notifications.detail.no_asks.note: Empty state under the asks header. Ends with a full stop.

mobile.notifications.detail.nothing_to_d.note: Empty state of the dismiss dialog when the conversation has no dismissable updates. Ends with a full stop.

mobile.notifications.detail.projects.note: Section header listing the projects a notification relates to.

mobile.notifications.dismiss.note: Accessibility label of the icon-only button that clears a notification from the inbox. Imperative.

mobile.notifications.filter_label.note: Accessible label of the segmented control that chooses which notifications are listed (unread or all). One word; a verb used as a label.

mobile.notifications.load_failed.note: Title of the error alert when the inbox could not be loaded. The relay's own sentence follows as the alert body.

mobile.notifications.permission.denied.note: Settings › Notifications, the state sentence when the OS refused notifications for the app. Names the remedy (system settings) and what it enables (Team Bridge message alerts), then that computer alerts are not switched on yet. Team Bridge is a brand.

mobile.notifications.permission.granted.note: Settings › Notifications, the state sentence after the reader allowed notifications. Two separate facts: Team Bridge (a brand, keep in Latin script) message alerts depend on Radient's (brand) push service being available, and alerts from the reader's computers are not switched on yet. Must not promise that alerts will definitely arrive.

mobile.notifications.permission.undeterm.note: Settings › Notifications, the state sentence before the OS has been asked; an 'Enable notifications' button sits under it. Team Bridge is a brand. Must not promise that alerts will definitely arrive.

mobile.notifications.permission.unknown.note: Settings › Notifications, the state sentence when the permission read failed. Must read as 'could not check', never as a refusal, and name the remedy (reopen Settings).

mobile.notifications.permission.unsuppor.note: Settings › Notifications, the state sentence when this app build or platform has no notification support (e.g. web). States a fact; offers no action.

mobile.notifications.priority_high.note: Badge on a notification the sender marked high priority. One word.

mobile.notifications.title.note: Title of the notifications inbox screen.
